source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Order of factors is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Recognize when two prime factorisations are the same despite a' is answered as order of factors rather than unique prime factorisation.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Same factorisation and product is what produces same prime factors with the same repetitions, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Recognize when two prime factorisations are the same.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is unique prime factorisation because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'Recognize when two prime factorisations are the same despite a' as the operative test.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: unique prime factorisation is settled by running 'Find a number's prime factorisation by breaking composite factors': Every number greater than 1 has a prime factorisation; keep replacing composite factors by — on the item about Recognize when two prime factorisations are the same.

intelligence.enrichment: A number has only one prime factorisation except for the order of the prime factors; multiplying the same primes in any order gives the same product.
